mainTopic: רבי עקיבא's safety in the פרדס, שדים and people, the forbidden areas of the משנה, secret sin, and the new משנה on סמיכה
overview: The גמרא first asks which פסוק רבי עקיבא learned from that kept him safe in the פרדס. Four אמוראים give four answers, each showing that God stands apart from His angels or is not found in the great forces around Him. Next comes a ברייתא that sorts שדים between angels and people, and people between angels and animals, with three traits on each side. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. It explains, with a parable of a palace built on a garbage dump, why one may not look into what came before creation. It then asks what 'not caring for the Maker's honor' means: staring at a rainbow (רבי אבא) or sinning in private (רב יוסף). A challenge from רבי אלעא הזקן is resolved by whether the person can control his יצר. Teachings of רבי יהודה בר רבי נחמני follow: three things one should not stare at, a warning not to trust the יצר הרע, and several views on who testifies against a secret sinner. The amud ends with a new משנה listing the pairs of leaders who argued about סמיכה on a קרבן.

steps.title: What did רבי עקיבא learn from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק רבי עקיבא expounded.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he expound?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: which פסוק did רבי עקיבא learn from? This sets up the four answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question picks up the earlier story of רבי עקיבא in the פרדס, who came out safely while אחר went wrong. It asks which lesson kept him safe. Three answers below are פסוקים showing that God stands apart from His angels. The fourth shows that God is not found in the great forces around Him.

keyTerms.meaning: He expounded, meaning he learned a lesson from a פסוק

phrases.english: What did he expound?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי עקיבא, from the story of the פרדס right before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the earlier story of רבי עקיבא in the פרדס.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק רבי עקיבא expounded that guided him in the פרדס.

steps.title: First answer: God is unique among His myriads
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, says the פסוק was "ואתא מרבבות קדש", read as: God is a sign, unique, among His myriads of angels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: "And He came from the holy myriads" means that He is unique among His myriads.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer gives the פסוק "ואתא מרבבות קדש" from דברים. The word ואתא is read like אות, a sign, to teach that God stands out as unique among all His angels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson comes from a play on words: ואתא, "and He came," sounds like אות, "a sign." So God is the one who stands out among the countless holy angels. With this in mind, רבי עקיבא would not mistake an angel for God.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy myriads, meaning tens of thousands of angels
A sign; something that stands out as unique
A myriad, ten thousand; a huge group

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
"And He came from the holy myriads"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:2. The word וְאָתָא (He came) sounds like אוֹת, a sign, and the next line builds on that.

phrases.english: He is a sign, unique, among His myriad.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ואתא מרבבות קדש, read as: God is unique among His myriads of angels.

steps.title: Second answer: God is the model among His myriad
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the פסוק was "דגול מרבבה", read as: God is the exemplary one among His myriad.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: "Preeminent above a myriad" means that He is the model among His myriad.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a different פסוק, "דגול מרבבה" from שיר השירים. He reads דגול like דוגמא, a model, so God is the outstanding one among His myriad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another play on words: דגול is read as דוגמא, an example or model. The idea matches the first answer, that God is above and different from all His angels, but it comes from a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Preeminent, outstanding; like a banner raised high

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:
"Preeminent above a myriad"
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 5:10.

phrases.english: He is the model among His myriad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק דגול מרבבה, read as: God is the model among His myriad.

steps.title: Third answer: God is the Master of His host
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the פסוק was "ה׳ צבאות שמו", read as: God is the Master over His host.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: "The Lord of hosts is His name" means that He is the Master in His host.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a third פסוק, "ה׳ צבאות שמו". It teaches that God is the Master who rules over all His heavenly armies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no play on words is needed: צבאות means hosts or armies, and God's name tells us He is their Lord. That means the angels serve under Him, and none of them should be mistaken for the Master.

keyTerms.meaning: Hosts or armies, here meaning the heavenly host of angels

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
"The Lord of hosts is His name"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 48:2.

phrases.english: He is the Master in His host.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ה׳ צבאות שמו, read as: God is the Master over His host.

steps.title: Fourth answer: God was not in the wind, earthquake or fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, says the פסוקים were the vision of אליהו: God was not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire, but there was a still, small voice, and "behold, God passed by."
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: "God was not in the wind. After the wind, an earthquake; God was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake, fire; God was not in the fire. After the fire, a still, small voice," and "behold, God passed by."
steps.whatsHappening: The last answer quotes the פסוקים from אליהו's vision in מלכים א. Great forces pass by, but God is not in them. He is found in the still, small voice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first three answers, this one does not read a single short phrase. It brings a whole scene teaching that powerful sights do not show where God is, so a person must know how to tell them apart from Him. This way רבי עקיבא could recognize where God's presence was and not cross into it.

keyTerms.meaning: A still, small voice; a thin, quiet sound

steps.whatToRemember: There are four answers to "מאי דרש": three פסוקים showing God is unique among, the model of, and Master over His angels, and the vision of אליהו showing that God is not found in the great forces around Him.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba
said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
"The Lord was not in the wind,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 19:11–12, from אליהו's vision at הר חורב.

phrases.english: and after the wind, an earthquake;
the Lord was not in the earthquake.
And after the earthquake, fire;
the Lord was not in the fire.
And after the fire, a still, small voice,"
and "behold, the Lord passed by."
phrases.notes: These words actually come earlier, at the start of the same scene (19:11). The גמרא adds them at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to the same question, using a whole scene instead of a short phrase.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים of אליהו's vision: God was not in the wind, earthquake or fire, and only after them came the still, small voice.

steps.title: Demons are like angels in three ways
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that six things are said about שדים: three make them like מלאכי השרת and three make them like people. It lists the three angel-like traits: wings, flying across the world, and knowing the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Six things were said about demons. In three ways they are like ministering angels, and in three ways they are like people. The three ways they are like angels: they have wings, they fly from one end of the world to the other, and they know what will happen in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sorts the traits of שדים into two groups. Here it lists the first group, the three ways they resemble מלאכי השרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up a pattern of six traits split three and three. This step gives only the angel-like half. The third trait, knowing the future, is about to be challenged by the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught. It opens a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Six things were said about demons:
three are like ministering angels,
and three are like human beings.
The three like ministering angels:
they have wings like ministering angels,

phrases.aramaic: וְטָסִין מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ כְּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת,
phrases.english: and they fly from one end of the world to the other like ministering angels,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹדְעִין מַה שֶּׁעָתִיד לִהְיוֹת כְּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת.
phrases.english: and they know what will happen in the future like ministering angels.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בַּשֵּׁדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about heavenly and in-between beings, after the discussion of God among His angels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שדים have three angel-like traits: wings, flying across the world, and knowledge of the future.

steps.title: Can demons really know the future?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that the ברייתא says שדים know the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it really enter your mind that they know the future?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ברייתא's claim that שדים know the future. This sets up the corrected reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that שדים 'know' the future sounds like they have real knowledge of what God plans. The גמרא finds that impossible, so it will reread the line in a weaker way.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? Said to show a claim is hard to accept.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not throwing out this trait. It only rejects the word 'know' and gives a softer version in the next line.

phrases.english: Could it enter your mind that they know?!
phrases.notes: He means: how could demons truly know the future on their own?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third angel-like trait listed in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that שדים know what will happen in the future.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real knowledge of the future is not something שדים could have, so the wording cannot be taken at face value.

steps.title: They overhear the future from behind the curtain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: שדים do not know the future, they hear it from behind the פרגוד, just like מלאכי השרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they hear it from behind the curtain, like ministering angels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the corrected meaning of the trait. שדים only overhear news of the future from behind the heavenly curtain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to angels stays, but it changes from 'knowing' to 'hearing.' Even the angels learn the future only when it is announced from behind the פרגוד, and שדים overhear it the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It brings a corrected reading.
The curtain. Here it means the heavenly curtain before God.

phrases.english: Rather, they hear from behind the curtain,
phrases.notes: Think of a curtain separating God from the heavenly beings. What is announced there gets overheard.

phrases.english: like ministering angels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by rereading the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שדים truly know the future on their own.
steps.terutzMaskana: שדים only overhear the future from behind the פרגוד, as the angels do.

steps.title: Demons are like people in three ways
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: שדים are like people in that they eat and drink, have children, and die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in three ways they are like people: they eat and drink like people, they have children like people, and they die like people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and finishes its list. It gives the three ways שדים are like human beings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the six traits of שדים. Their physical needs and their death place them with people, not with angels.

keyTerms.meaning: They multiply, meaning they have children

steps.whatToRemember: שדים are in-between beings: like angels in wings, flying, and overhearing the future, and like people in eating and drinking, having children, and dying.

phrases.english: And the three like human beings:
they eat and drink like human beings,
they multiply like human beings,
and they die like human beings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the correction in steps 7 and 8 to finish the ברייתא's list from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שדים have three human-like traits: eating and drinking, having children, and dying.

steps.title: People are like angels in three ways
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now teaches six things about people: three like מלאכי השרת and three like animals. The three angel-like traits are understanding, walking upright, and speaking לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six things were said about people. In three ways they are like ministering angels, and in three ways they are like animals. The three ways like angels: they have understanding, they walk standing upright, and they speak in the holy language.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the same six-trait pattern, now for human beings. This step lists the three ways people are like מלאכי השרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People are now placed between angels above and animals below, just as שדים were placed between angels and people. The angel-like traits here are mind, upright posture, and speech in לשון הקודש.

phrases.english: Six things were said about human beings:
three are like ministering angels, three are like animals.
The three like ministering angels:
they have understanding like ministering angels,
and they walk upright like ministering angels,
and they speak in the holy language like ministering angels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same six-trait pattern from the ברייתא about שדים, now applied to people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People have three angel-like traits: understanding, upright posture, and speaking לשון הקודש.

steps.title: People are like animals in three ways
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: people are like animals in that they eat and drink, have children, and produce waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: In three ways they are like animals: they eat and drink like animals, they have children like animals, and they produce waste like animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list about people. It gives the three ways human beings are like animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of these traits, eating and drinking and having children, are the same ones that made שדים like people. The new trait is producing waste, and it places people with animals.
steps.whatToRemember: Each kind of being sits between two others. שדים are between angels and people, and people are between angels and animals, with three traits on each side.

phrases.english: The three like animals:
they eat and drink like animals,
and they multiply like animals,
and they produce waste like animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the six traits of people begun in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People have three animal-like traits: eating and drinking, having children, and producing waste.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Looking Into Four Things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that whoever looks into four things would have been better off never being born.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever looks into four things, it would have been better for him had he never come into the world, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה to set up a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists four forbidden areas to think about: what is above, what is below, what was before creation, and what will be after. The גמרא quotes only the opening and writes 'etc.' because it is about to ask about one of the four.

keyTerms.meaning: One who looks into or thinks deeply about something
It would have been better for him
Etc. The quote continues beyond these words

phrases.english: Whoever looks into four things

phrases.aramaic: רָתוּי לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: it would have been better for him had he not come into the world, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the four things: what is above, below, before, and after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא about שדים and people is finished. The גמרא now goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Looking into the four forbidden areas (above, below, before, after) is so bad that it would have been better never to be born.

steps.title: Why Is Thinking About 'Before' Forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why above, below, and after are forbidden, but asks why 'before creation' is forbidden, since it already happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for what is above, what is below, and what is after. But before? What happened, happened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts three of the four forbidden areas but challenges the fourth: why can't you think about what came before the world?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above, below, and after are things outside our world, so it is clear why they are off-limits. But the time before creation is past history and already over. So why should it be dangerous to think about it?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces the part that is understood)

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding what is above,
what is below, and what is after,
that is fine.
But before,
what happened, happened?
phrases.notes: He means: it's already over, so what harm is there in thinking about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מָה לְמַעְלָה מָה לְמַטָּה מָה לְאָחוֹר לְחַיֵּי אֶלָּא לְפָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one item from the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on thinking about what came before creation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The past is already finished, so there seems to be no reason to forbid thinking about it, unlike the other three areas.

steps.title: The Parable of the Palace on the Garbage Dump
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר explain with a parable: a king who built a palace on a garbage dump does not want the dump mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both say: It is like a human king who told his servants, 'Build me large palaces on the garbage dump.' They went and built them for him. The king does not want anyone to mention the garbage dump.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question with a parable. Thinking about what came before creation is like bringing up the dump the king's palace was built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not that the past is dangerous to know. It is a matter of honor. Just as a king is embarrassed when people mention the dump under his palace, ה׳ does not want people dwelling on the chaos that came before His beautiful world.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on thinking about 'before creation' is about respecting ה׳'s honor, like not mentioning the dump under a king's palace.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar both say:
It is like a flesh-and-blood king
who said to his servants:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוּ לִי פַּלְטֵירִין גְּדוֹלִין עַל הָאַשְׁפָּה.
phrases.english: Build me large palaces on the garbage dump.
They went and built them for him.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ לְהַזְכִּיר שֵׁם אַשְׁפָּה.
phrases.english: The king does not want the garbage dump to be mentioned.
phrases.notes: The world is the palace. The chaos before creation is the dump it was built on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason behind the rule through a parable.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The past is finished, so thinking about it should be harmless.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is disrespectful to ה׳ to dwell on the chaos His world was built upon.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Not Caring for the Maker's Honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: whoever does not care for his Maker's honor would have been better off never being born.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever does not care about the honor of his Maker, it would have been better for him had he never come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the משנה to set up a question about what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new clause of the משנה. It is very vague. It does not say what kind of behavior counts as 'not caring for the Maker's honor,' so the גמרא will ask.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁלֹּא חָס עַל כְּבוֹד קוֹנוֹ,
phrases.english: Whoever does not care about the honor of his Maker,
it would have been better for him had he not come into the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שֶׁלֹּא חָס עַל כְּבוֹד קוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who does not care for ה׳'s honor would have been better off never being born.

steps.title: What Does This Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what behavior the משנה is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition: what exactly counts as not caring about the Maker's honor?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a general phrase with no example. The גמרא wants to know the specific act being described.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for a definition)

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the phrase just quoted from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What specific act counts as 'not caring for the honor of one's Maker.'

steps.title: Two Answers: Looking at a Rainbow or Sinning in Private
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says it means staring at a rainbow. רב יוסף says it means sinning in private.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: This is someone who looks at the rainbow. רב יוסף said: This is someone who sins in private.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא picks an act that disrespects a sign of ה׳'s glory. רב יוסף picks a sin done in secret. The next two steps give the reason and source for each view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
This is one who looks at the rainbow.
Rav Yosef said:
This is one who commits a sin in private.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר זֶה הַמִּסְתַּכֵּל בַּקֶּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבא: staring at a rainbow. רב יוסף: sinning in private.

steps.title: Why the Rainbow: It Looks Like ה׳'s Glory
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives רבי אבא's source: יחזקאל compares the rainbow to the appearance of ה׳'s glory.
steps.simpleTranslation: Looking at the rainbow, as it is written: 'Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on a rainy day, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אבא's view by quoting a פסוק that links the rainbow to ה׳'s glory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יחזקאל describes ה׳'s glory as looking like a rainbow. So staring at a rainbow is like staring at a likeness of ה׳'s glory, which is disrespectful.

phrases.english: One who looks at the rainbow,
as it is written:
"Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 1:28

phrases.english: on the day of rain,
so was the appearance of the brightness all around.
This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for רבי אבא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's claim that staring at a rainbow disrespects ה׳.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 1:28, which compares ה׳'s glory to a rainbow.

steps.title: Why Sinning in Private: Pushing Away ה׳'s Feet
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's view is based on רבי יצחק: sinning in private is like pushing away the feet of the שכינה, since the earth is ה׳'s footstool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is one who sins in private, like רבי יצחק. For רבי יצחק said: Whoever sins in private, it is as if he pushes away the feet of the שכינה, as it says: 'So says ה׳: The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב יוסף's view by bringing a teaching of רבי יצחק with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who sins in private acts as if no one sees him, as if ה׳ is not there. But the פסוק says the whole earth is ה׳'s footstool. So acting this way is like pushing ה׳'s feet out of that place.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the view of רבי יצחק
Pushes away the feet of the Divine Presence

steps.whatToRemember: Not caring for ה׳'s honor = staring at a rainbow (רבי אבא) or sinning in private as if ה׳ is not there (רב יוסף).

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
This is one who commits a sin in private,
in line with Rabbi Yitzchak.
For Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Whoever commits a sin in private,
it is as if he pushes away the feet of the Divine Presence,
as it says:
"So says the Lord: The heavens are My throne
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 66:1

phrases.english: and the earth is My footstool."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר זֶה הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה בַּסֵּתֶר כִּדְרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי אבא's view, the גמרא now explains רב יוסף's view.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that sinning in private disrespects ה׳.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק's teaching, based on ישעיהו 66:1 (the earth is ה׳'s footstool).

steps.title: Challenge from רבי אלעא הזקן: sinning in private can be the better choice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how sinning in private can be so terrible when רבי אלעא הזקן advises a person overcome by his יצר to sin privately rather than cause a public חילול ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי אלעא הזקן said: If a person sees that his יצר is overpowering him, he should go to a place where nobody knows him. He should dress in black, wrap himself in black, and do what his heart desires, but he should not desecrate ה׳'s Name in public!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's explanation from step 17, that the משנה is talking about someone who sins in private. It quotes a teaching that seems to recommend sinning in private.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said sinning in private is like pushing away the שכינה, which is very severe. But רבי אלעא הזקן presents private sinning as the lesser evil compared to a public חילול ה׳. So how can private sinning be the thing the משנה condemns so harshly?

keyTerms.meaning: his inclination, his urge to sin
black clothing, worn like a mourner

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעא הזקן is not giving permission to sin. He is telling a person who is about to sin anyway how to at least avoid the much worse damage of a public חילול ה׳. The black clothes are meant to humble him, and they may even stop him.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rabbi Ila the Elder say:

phrases.aramaic: אִם רוֹאֶה אָדָם שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו
phrases.english: If a person sees that his inclination is overpowering him
he should go to a place where people do not recognize him,
and wear black and wrap himself in black,
and do what his heart desires,
but let him not desecrate the Name of Heaven in public!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's view, which was just explained in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that sinning in private shows no care for ה׳'s honor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעא הזקן treats private sinning as preferable to public sinning, so it cannot be the worst kind of disrespect

steps.title: Answer: it depends on whether he can control his יצר
steps.stepSummary: Someone who can overcome his יצר and sins in private anyway is the one the משנה condemns. רבי אלעא's advice is only for someone who truly cannot overcome it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difficulty. רב יוסף's case is where the person is able to bend his יצר. רבי אלעא's case is where he is not able to bend his יצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two statements describe two different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person could resist but chooses to sin quietly, that is the disrespect רב יוסף meant. If he truly cannot resist, the advice is to at least keep it private and avoid a public חילול ה׳. Both views now stand.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (two cases are different)

steps.whatToRemember: Sinning in private is condemned when a person could have resisted. The advice to go somewhere far away is only for someone who truly cannot overcome his יצר.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is where he is able to bend his inclination,
phrases.notes: "This" is רב יוסף's case, the person who sins privately even though he could have held back.

phrases.english: that is where he is not able to bend his inclination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements seemed to clash about how bad private sinning is
steps.terutzMaskana: Private sinning is condemned when a person could have resisted. It is the lesser evil only when he could not.

steps.title: Three things that make the eyes grow dim
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר רבי נחמני teaches that gazing at the rainbow, the נשיא, or the כהנים makes one's eyes grow dim.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה son of רבי נחמני, the spokesman of ריש לקיש, taught: Whoever gazes at three things, his eyes grow dim: the rainbow, the נשיא, and the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching linked to רבי אבא's idea that staring at a rainbow is disrespectful. It lists three things a person should not stare at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This widens the idea from step 17. The rainbow is not the only thing a person should not stare at. All three reflect ה׳'s glory in some way, as the next step will show.

keyTerms.meaning: his spokesman, who announced the teacher's words to the crowd
the leader of the Jewish people

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Nachmani expounded,
the spokesman of Reish Lakish:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמִּסְתַּכֵּל בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים עֵינָיו כֵּהוֹת:
phrases.english: Whoever gazes at three things, his eyes grow dim:
at the rainbow, at the Nasi, and at the kohanim.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי נַחְמָנִי מְתוּרְגְּמָנֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching connected to רבי אבא's rainbow idea
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gazing at the rainbow, the נשיא, or the כהנים dims one's eyes

steps.title: Sources for each of the three things
steps.stepSummary: The rainbow resembles ה׳'s glory, the נשיא carries ה׳'s splendor, and the כהנים blessed with the שם המפורש in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rainbow, as it is written: "Like the appearance of the bow in the cloud on a rainy day... this was the appearance of the likeness of ה׳'s glory." The נשיא, as it is written: "And you shall put some of your splendor upon him." And the כהנים means one who gazes at them while the בית המקדש stands, when they would stand on their platform and bless Israel with the שם המפורש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each of the three things should not be stared at. It gives a פסוק for the rainbow and for the נשיא, and it explains when the rule about the כהנים applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item carries something of ה׳'s glory. For the rainbow and the נשיא this comes from a פסוק. For the כהנים the rule is limited to the time of the בית המקדש, when they blessed with the שם המפורש.

keyTerms.meaning: their platform, where the כהנים stood to bless

phrases.english: At the rainbow, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״כְּמַרְאֵה הַקֶּשֶׁת אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בֶעָנָן בְּיוֹם הַגֶּשֶׁם
phrases.english: "Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on a rainy day
this was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 1:28, the same פסוק רבי אבא used back in step 18.

phrases.english: At the Nasi, as it is written:
"And you shall put some of your splendor upon him."
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:20

phrases.aramaic: הַמִּסְתַּכֵּל בַּכֹּהֲנִים בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים,
phrases.english: And one who gazes at the kohanim means at the time the Temple is standing,
when they would stand on their platform
and bless Israel with the explicit Name.
phrases.notes: The explicit Name means ה׳'s special Name said out loud exactly as it is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources and the scope for the three items listed in step 22
steps.raayaObject: The three items that dim the eyes
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 1:28, במדבר 27:20, and the כהנים blessing with the שם המפורש in the בית המקדש

steps.title: Do not believe the יצר הרע when it says ה׳ will forgive
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר רבי נחמני reads the פסוק in מיכה as a warning not to trust the יצר הרע's promise that ה׳ will forgive any sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה son of רבי נחמני, the spokesman of ריש לקיש, taught: What is the meaning of the פסוק "Do not trust a friend, do not rely on a chief"? If the יצר הרע tells you, "Sin, and הקב"ה will forgive," do not believe it, as it says: "Do not trust a friend."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same רבי יהודה. He explains a פסוק as a warning against the יצר הרע's trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יצר הרע tries to make sinning feel safe by pointing to ה׳'s mercy. The פסוק says not to trust this reasoning. The next step shows how the פסוק's words point to the יצר הרע and to הקב"ה.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Nachmani expounded,
the spokesman of Reish Lakish:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Do not trust a friend, do not rely on a chief"?
phrases.notes: מיכה 7:5

phrases.english: If the evil inclination says to you,
"Sin, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, will forgive,"
do not believe it,
as it is said: "Do not trust a friend."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי נַחְמָנִי מְתוּרְגְּמָנֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by the same רבי יהודה, connected to the theme of private sinning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not trust the יצר הרע's claim that ה׳ will forgive whatever you do

steps.title: Proving what "רֵעַ" and "אַלּוּף" mean
steps.stepSummary: The word רֵעַ points to the יצר הרע, which the Torah calls רַע. The word אַלּוּף means הקב"ה, as ירמיהו calls ה׳ "אלוף נעורי".
steps.simpleTranslation: "רע" means only the יצר הרע, as it says: "For the inclination of man's heart is evil." And "אלוף" means only הקב"ה, as it says: "You are the guide of my youth."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the reading of the pasuk by showing from other פסוקים what each word refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With these two definitions, the פסוק reads: do not trust the יצר הרע when it tells you to rely on הקב"ה's forgiveness. Each word is defined by another פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: and ... refers to nothing other than

phrases.english: And "ra" refers to nothing other than the evil inclination,
phrases.notes: The פסוק says רֵעַ, meaning friend, but the גמרא reads it like רַע, meaning evil.

phrases.english: as it is said: "For the inclination of man's heart is evil."
phrases.notes: בראשית 8:21

phrases.english: And "aluf" refers to nothing other than the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is said: "You are the guide of my youth."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of the pasuk given in step 24
steps.raayaObject: The meanings of רֵעַ and אַלּוּף in the pasuk in מיכה

steps.title: But who will testify against me in private?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא imagines a sinner thinking that nobody sees him, so nobody can testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you will say: Who will testify against me?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא raises the sinner's excuse so that it can answer it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the theme of sinning in private. A person might think that with no witnesses, nobody will ever know. The answer comes right after.

phrases.english: Perhaps you will say: Who will testify against me?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible excuse against the warning in steps 24 and 25
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who could testify against a sin done in secret?

steps.title: The stones and beams of his house testify
steps.stepSummary: Even in private, the stones and beams of a person's own house testify against him, as the pasuk in חבקוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stones and beams of a person's house testify against him, as it says: "For a stone from the wall will cry out, and a beam from the wood will answer it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the sinner's excuse. Nothing is truly hidden, because his very house is a witness against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to רב יוסף's point that sinning in private is still a serious offense. Even without human witnesses, the sin is recorded and known.
steps.whatToRemember: There is no such thing as a truly secret sin. Do not believe the יצר הרע when it says ה׳ will simply forgive, and do not think private sins go unnoticed.

phrases.aramaic: אַבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ וְקוֹרוֹת בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
phrases.english: The stones of a person's house and the beams of his house,
they testify against him,
as it is said: "For a stone from the wall will cry out,
and a beam from the wood will answer it."
phrases.notes: חבקוק 2:11

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ וְקוֹרוֹת בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הֵם מְעִידִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The stones and beams of his own house testify against him, based on חבקוק 2:11

steps.title: The Sages say the person's own soul testifies
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים give another answer to the sinner who thinks nobody saw him: his own נשמה will testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: a person's נשמה testifies against him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the sinner who thinks no one saw him. The חכמים say his own soul will be the witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said the stones and beams of his house testify. The חכמים go further: the witness is inside the person himself. The proof comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
A person's soul testifies against him

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: נִשְׁמָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מְעִידָה בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than step 27 to the question in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who testifies against a sinner when no person saw him?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His own soul testifies against him.

steps.title: Proof from מיכה: the one lying in your bosom is the soul
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in מיכה warns to guard your mouth from 'the one who lies in your bosom.' The only thing that lives inside a person is the נשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'From the one who lies in your bosom, guard the doors of your mouth.' What thing dwells in a person's bosom? You must say: this is the soul.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים prove their view from a פסוק. They ask what 'lies in your bosom,' and answer that it must be the soul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק warns you to be careful even in front of 'the one in your bosom,' meaning someone who could report on you. Since the soul is the thing that lives inside a person, the soul is the one who can testify.

keyTerms.meaning: you must say, it can only be

phrases.english: As it says: "From the one who lies in your bosom
guard the doors of your mouth"
phrases.notes: מיכה 7:5

phrases.english: (Which thing lies)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.aramaic: [אֵי זֶה הוּא דָּבָר שֶׁשָּׁרוּי] בְּחֵיקוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם —
phrases.english: [What thing dwells] in a person's bosom?
You must say: this is the soul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the פסוק that supports the חכמים in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That the soul testifies against a person
steps.raayaSupportSource: מיכה 7:5, 'From the one who lies in your bosom, guard the doors of your mouth'

steps.title: רבי זריקא: the two escorting angels testify
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא says the two מלאכי השרת who go with every person are the witnesses, proven from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא says: the two מלאכי השרת who accompany him, they testify against him, as it says: 'For He will command His angels for you, to guard you in all your ways.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זריקא gives a third answer. Every person has two angels with him, and they testify about what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳'s angels guard a person 'in all your ways,' so they are always with him. Since they are there for everything he does, they can testify even when no human saw.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika says:
The two ministering angels who accompany him,
they testify against him,
as it says: "For He will command His angels for you
to guard you in all your ways."
phrases.notes: תהלים 91:11

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת הַמְלַוִּין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the question of step 26, different from the stones and the soul.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who testifies against a sinner when no person saw him?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two angels who accompany him testify.

steps.title: Another view of the Sages: a person's own limbs testify
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say a person's own limbs testify against him, from the פסוק 'You are My witnesses' in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: a person's limbs testify against him, as it says: 'And you are My witnesses, says ה׳, and I am God.'
steps.whatsHappening: A final answer: the person's own body parts will be the witnesses against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'you are My witnesses,' which is read as the person himself being the witness. So the very limbs he used to sin become the testimony against him.
steps.whatToRemember: Four answers to the sinner who thinks no one saw: the stones of his house, his soul, his two angels, and his own limbs. Every view says there is always a witness.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
A person's limbs testify against him,
as it says: "And you are My witnesses,
says ה׳, and I am God."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 43:12. Read it as: you yourselves, your own bodies, are the witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵבָרָיו שֶׁל אָדָם מְעִידִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last answer in the list of who testifies, closing this aggadic section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who testifies against a sinner when no person saw him?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His own limbs testify against him.

steps.title: New משנה: four pairs of leaders argue about סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists pairs of leaders from each generation; in each pair one says not to do סמיכה and the other says to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: יוסי בן יועזר says not to lean hands; יוסף בן יוחנן says to lean. יהושע בן פרחיה says not to lean; ניתאי הארבלי says to lean. יהודה בן טבאי says not to lean; שמעון בן שטח says to lean. שמעיה says to lean; אבטליון says not to lean.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה starts. It lists four pairs of leaders, one pair per generation, who argued about whether to do סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה simply lists who held which side, pair after pair. Notice the order flips with שמעיה and אבטליון: here the first one says to lean and the second says not to.

keyTerms.meaning: to lean one's hands on a קרבן (סמיכה)
leaning hands on an animal before it is brought as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: This סמיכה is leaning hands on a קרבן, not the סמיכה of giving rabbinic ordination.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
phrases.english: Yosei ben Yo'ezer says not to lean hands,
phrases.notes: This is about leaning hands on a קרבן on יום טוב, since leaning on the animal may count as using it on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Yosef ben Yochanan says to lean.

phrases.aramaic: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָה אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
phrases.english: Yehoshua ben Perachya says not to lean,
Nitai HaArbeli says to lean.

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בֶּן טָבַאי אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
phrases.english: Yehuda ben Tabbai says not to lean,
Shimon ben Shatach says to lean.
Shemaya says to lean,
Avtalyon says not to lean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and begins a new משנה on a new subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In each generation one leader held not to do סמיכה and the other held to do it.

steps.title: הלל and מנחם agreed; then שמאי replaced מנחם and argued
steps.stepSummary: הלל and מנחם did not argue. When מנחם left and שמאי took his place, שמאי said not to lean and הלל said to lean.
steps.simpleTranslation: הלל and מנחם did not disagree. מנחם left, שמאי entered. שמאי says not to lean; הלל says to lean.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with the last generation. At first הלל and מנחם agreed, but after שמאי replaced מנחם, the argument came back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This pair is different: for a time there was no dispute at all. Once מנחם left his position and שמאי entered, שמאי took the side of not leaning, and הלל held to lean.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists five generations of pairs arguing about סמיכה; only הלל and מנחם agreed, until שמאי replaced מנחם.

phrases.english: Hillel and Menachem did not disagree.
Menachem left, Shammai entered.
Shammai says not to lean,
Hillel says to lean.
